Subject (in full) Discovery of communist literature at No.471 Tong Sheo Fung
(東壽坊), Range Road, on 26.1.34.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by O.B.Ku. D.I.

With reference to the attached file on the finding of
a quantity of communist literature at No.471 Tong Sheo Fung (東壽坊)
Range Road, on 26.1.34, which was later ascertained by the
Municipal Police as being the home of a communist agent named
Bah Tung (伯 釗) who had been arrested by the Municipal Police
at 1338 Haining Road on 12.1.34 on the authority of a warrant
issued at the instance of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau.
He was extradited to the Chinese Authorities by Court order on
January 20, 1934.

Exhaustive enquiries made from the local Kuomintang
Headquarters through Supt. Tan Shao-liang finally ascertained
from Mr. Loh Yuen-fu, an officer attached to the Investigation
Department of the local Kuomintang Headquarters, that the communist
literature in question was on 5.2.34 handed over to the local
Kuomintang Authorities by order of the Second Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court for investigation and on 8.2.34 the same court sent
a notification to the local Kuomintang Authorities requesting
that the literature together with the result of findings be
transmitted to the local Public Safety Bureau to be used as
evidence in the case against Bah Tung. This request was
acceded to on March 5, 1934.

The local Kuomintang Headquarters, upon completing its
investigation, discovered that, apart from a book (two volumes)
entitled "History of Imperialist Oppression of China," which is
of an anti-Imperialist nature, the remaining literature was
purely communist propaganda.

In view of the fact that the literature has been handed
over direct to the Public Safety Bureau, it is unnecessary for
the Municipal Police to pursue this matter further.

关于附件中提及的于1934年1月26日在虹口路東壽坊471号发现大量共产主义文献一事，后经工部局警务处查明，该处系一名名为 Bah Tung (伯釗) 的共产党特工的住所。此人曾根据上海市公安局的请求签发的逮捕令，于1934年1月12日被工部局警务处在海宁路1338号逮捕。他于1934年1月20日经法院命令引渡给中国当局。

通过谭绍良 (Tan Shao-liang) 巡官向当地国民党总部进行的详尽查询，最终从当地国民党总部调查科官员罗元福 (Loh Yuen-fu) 先生处获悉，上述共产主义文献已于1934年2月5日奉江苏高等法院第二分院之命移交给当地国民党当局进行调查；1934年2月8日，该法院又向当地国民党当局发出通知，要求将该批文献连同调查结果一并移送当地公安局，作为起诉 Bah Tung 一案的证据。此项请求已于1934年3月5日获准执行。

REPORT
Date Jan. 27th 19 34
Subject (in full) Discovery of Communistic literature at No.471 Tong Sheo Fung, off Range Road on the 26-1-34
Made by D. S. Self Forwarded by

Sir,
At about 10-15.p.m. 26-1-34 a Chinese female, Hsi Lu Sa, (徐陸氏 東春坊 ) housemistress of a dwelling house at No.471 Tong Sheo Fung, off Range Road, came to the station and reported that on the 23-12-33 a male Chinese, description below :-
Name given as "Hsi" ( 錢 ) age about 20. Slim build. Height about 5' 2" Native of Canton. Speaking Northern and Cantonese dialects. Wearing dark Sun-Yat-Sen uniform.
engaged the downstairs back room at her house for the monthly rental of $4-50cts.
The lodger was last seen on the 6-1-34, after which date he failed to return to the house. On the 26-1-34 at about 8.p.m. the informant noticed that the lock securing the room door had been removed and the place entered. Fearing that a theft had been committed the housemistress thought it advisable to report the affair to the station.
The undersigned together with C. D. S. 259 visited the address in question when a search of the room disclosed a quantity of Anti-Government and Communistic literature. This literature was brought to the station and Sub-Inspector Everest of the Special Branch informed. This officer gave instructions that the literature be sent to the Special Branch for examination. This was done on the morning of the 27-1-34.
Other property remaining in the room was also brought to the station, (list attached) It will be subsequently sent to the Court for disposal.
The housemistress states that her lodger often had visitors and when visitors did call they were closely closeted with the man.
She has been instructed how to act should he return.

D.D.O. "C" Div.
Senior Det.
A. Self

事由（全称） 1934年1月26日在靶子路通寿坊471号发现共产主义文献
呈报人 D. S. Self 转呈人

先生，
1934年1月26日晚约10点15分，一名中国妇女徐陆氏（东春坊），系靶子路通寿坊471号一处住宅的女房东，来到捕房报案称，1933年12月23日，一名中国男子，特征如下：-
自报姓名为“钱”(Hsi)，年龄约20岁。身材瘦削。身高约5英尺2英寸。广东籍。讲北方话和粤语。身穿深色中山装。
以每月租金4.50美元租下了她家楼下的后间。
该住客最后被人看见是在1934年1月6日，此后便未回寓所。1934年1月26日晚约8点，报案人发现锁住房门的锁已被拆除，有人进入屋内。女房东担心发生盗窃，认为宜向捕房报告此事。
卑职会同警员编号259前往上述地址，经搜查房间，发现了大量反政府和共产主义文献。这些文献被带回捕房，并通知了特别处的艾弗勒斯特（Everest）副督察。该警官指示将文献送往特别处进行检查。此项工作已于1934年1月27日上午完成。
房间内遗留的其他物品也被带回捕房（附清单）。随后将送交法庭处理。
女房东称，她的住客常有访客，每当有访客到来，他们便与该男子密谈。
已指示她若该男子返回应如何应对。

C区代理巡官
高级侦探
A. Self

Now and then during the conversation Koh Ying requested Bah
Tung to express his opinion. I heard Koh Ying talk and saw
her taking notes (on another piece of paper).

seemed to be well acquainted with Koh Ying. On seeing Koo,

What is the Soviet?

The Soviet is the motherland of labourers and farmers.
It was first established in Russia. At present, Soviet

Soviet China include Hupeh, Hunan, Fukien, Kiangsi,

What is the Red Army?

The Red Army is the defender of the motherland of

Why is the Red Army strong?

The victory of the Red Army will mean the expansion

The Red Army has the strong support of farmers and labourers.
These are some of the reasons why the Red Army is strong.

Life in the Red Army

The Red Army has free clubs. There they can read, play
and talk. Through reading and unhindered discussion, they
can understand the situation in the world and thus learn
how the capitalists and landlords are oppressing the peasant
and labour masses. They will also realise how the progress

什么是苏维埃？

苏维埃是劳工和农民的祖国。它最初建立于俄国。目前，苏维埃区域也在中国发展。

苏维埃中国包括湖北、湖南、福建、江西、广东和江西省。现在已明确将四川省染红。

什么是红军？

红军是劳工和农民祖国的保卫者。它正在与资本家和地主作战。

红军为何强大？

红军的胜利意味着苏维埃区域的扩大，这将给农民和劳工的家庭带来幸福。在满洲，日本帝国主义者正在与由农民和劳工组成的部队作战。日本的这些农民和劳工家庭无法从日本的胜利中获得任何利益，他们的生活状况将每况愈下。在红军中，官兵之间从未有过摩擦。红军的指挥官是从劳工和农民中选拔出来的。他们住在一起，吃同样的食物，穿同样的衣服。红军得到农民和劳工的强力支持。这些就是红军强大的部分原因。

红军设有自由俱乐部。在那里他们可以阅读、玩耍和交谈。通过阅读和不受阻碍的讨论，他们可以了解世界局势，从而了解资本家和地主是如何压迫农民和劳工大众的。他们还将认识到，如果国民党被推翻，帝国主义者的进展

"Address to sailor brothers" on the occasion of the 6th
anniversary of the Canton Uprising of December 11

December 11. This is the day when the Soviet Government
was established in Canton following upon the defeat of the
capitalists, landlords and militarists who were oppressing
labourers, farmers and soldiers in Canton. Unfortunately,
the government was dissolved by armed forces of Japanese,
British and American Imperialists. But the Soviet districts
have made remarkable expansion since then. The Red Army
is protecting labourers, peasants and soldiers by gaining
victories over the government troops. The 5th Anti-Communist
Campaign organized by Chiang Kai-shek has ended in failure.

What was the cause of the defeat of the Soviet Government
at Canton? It was because the militarists and imperialists
were then more powerful than the Soviet, and the labour and
peasant masses did not know how to use the arms which they
had seized from the militarists. Unless earnest support is
given by soldiers, the overthrow of the capitalists and
landlords cannot be effected.

Dear sailor brothers. By protecting the families
of labourers, farmers and the working masses with your
rifles and swords, you can emancipate the oppressed people
in Japan as well as in other countries. The ruling classes
such as the capitalists, the landlords and the officers
are trying to employ you to massacre our comrades at Hankow,
Shanghai and Manchuria.

Protect the peasant and labour masses.

Direct your guns at the capitalists and landlords.

Koh Ying (郭英)
Nanking                                S.S.I. Prokofiev
W. Hongkew Stn        13-1-34                  Clerk Fang Kuo Tien

My name is Koh Ying (郭英), age 21, native of
Nanking, unemployed.    I first arrived in Shanghai from
Nanking where I studied in a middle school until the summer
of 1932, after which I lived there with my parents. I have
since been living with my cousin named Koh Miao (郭淼) at
No.63 Ko Loh Li (戈登路), Av. Edward VII, French Concession.
My cousin is the proprietor of the Chung Mei Printing Company
(中美) at that address.    About two weeks ago a friend
of mine named Wong Ying (王英) introduced me to one named
Zung (宗) who I understand is a teacher.    Zung told me
that he would try to find a position as teacher for me. I
visited Zung at his house No.1338, Lane 945, Haining Road,
three or four times.    I did not meet anybody at his house
until the evening of 12/1/34 when I found him in company with
another man.    It was about 6 p.m.    Shortly afterwards two
more men arrived.    I never saw any of these three men before
and do not know their names.    Zung and I talked about the
possibility of getting a position for me. At about 7 p.m. Zung
went out to order some food for us and while he was absent
the Police came and we were all arrested.

I do not know the reason of my arrest. I do not
belong to the Communist or any other political party. I know
nothing about the books and pamphlets seized by the Police in
the room.    I think they belong to Zung.

(Signed) Koh Ying.

郭英 (Koh Ying)
南京                                副督察 普罗科菲耶夫 (S.S.I. Prokofiev)
西虹口巡捕房        1934年1月13日                  书记员 方国田 (Fang Kuo Tien)

我叫郭英，21岁，南京人，无业。我最初从南京来到上海，在南京的一所中学读书直到1932年夏天，之后我与父母住在那里。此后我一直与我的表亲郭淼（Koh Miao）住在法租界爱多亚路戈登路（Ko Loh Li）63号。我的表亲是该地址中美印刷公司（Chung Mei Printing Company）的老板。大约两周前，我的一位名叫王英（Wong Ying）的朋友将我介绍给一位名叫宗（Zung）的人，据我了解他是一名教师。宗告诉我，他会尽力为我找一个教师的职位。我曾去过三次或四次他在海宁路945弄1338号的住所。在他家里我没有遇到任何人，直到1934年1月12日晚上，我发现他和另一个男人在一起。大约是下午6点。不久之后，又有两个男人到达。我以前从未见过这三个人，也不知道他们的名字。宗和我谈论了为我谋取职位的可能性。大约晚上7点，宗出去为我们订购食物，当他不在时，警察来了，我们都被捕了。

我不知道我被捕的原因。我不属于共产党或任何其他政党。我对警察在房间里查获的书籍和小册子一无所知。我想它们属于宗。

（签名）郭英。

Koo Ah Shing (顧阿興)
Pootung                                      D.S.I. Prokofiev
W.Hongkew Stn        13-1-34                 Clerk Pang Kuo Liang

My name is Koo Ah Shing, agr 17, native of Pootung,
unemployed printer. From the age of 6 to 10 years I studied
at a private school in my native place, after which I assisted
my father in farming work. At the age of 13 I started to work
as an apprentice at a printing establishment in Pootung. I
then came to Shanghai and worked at the Commercial Press for
about 3 months when I was dismissed owing to the reduction of
staff. I returned to my native place and have since been
working on my father's farm. On January 7, 1934, I came to
Shanghai from my native place in order to find some employment
here. I lived in various small lodging houses situated in
the vicinity of the Great World, French Concession. I do
not know the location of the lodging houses. At about 6 p.m.
12-1-34 I went to No.1538 lane 945, Haining Road, to visit my
friend named Zung (曾) who is a teacher at some school in
Shanghai. I met Zung about 8 years when I was employed at
the Commercial Press. Zung promised me to find work. Apart
from Zung there were one female and two males in the room. I
never saw these people before and I do not know their names.
Zung and I had a talk about the possibility of finding a job
for me. He then went out saying he would get some food for us.
while he was absent the Police arrived and arrested all those
present in the room.

I know nothing about the books and pamphlets seized by
the Police in the room. I think they belong to Zung. He never
gave me any book to read. I am not a communist and do not
belong to any political party.

(Signed) Koo Ah Shing.

我叫顾阿兴，17岁，浦东人，失业印刷工。从6岁到10岁，我在家乡的私塾读书，之后协助父亲从事农活。13岁时，我开始在浦东的一家印刷所做学徒。后来我来到上海，在商务印书馆工作了大约3个月，后因裁员被解雇。我回到家乡，此后一直在父亲的农场工作。1934年1月7日，我从家乡来到上海，以便在这里寻找工作。我住在法租界大世界附近的各种小旅馆里。我不知道这些旅馆的具体位置。1934年1月12日下午6点左右，我去海宁路945弄1538号拜访我的朋友曾（Zung，注：此处原文拼音为Zung，中文名写作曾，与前文郑子年/郑子仪不同，依原文翻译），他是上海某学校的教师。我大约在8年前在商务印书馆工作时认识了曾。曾答应帮我找工作。除了曾之外，房间里还有一名女性和两名男性。我以前从未见过这些人，也不知道他们的名字。曾和我谈了为我找工作的可能性。然后他出去了，说要去给我们弄点吃的。当他不在时，警察到达并逮捕了房间里的所有人。

我对警察在房间里查获的书籍和小册子一无所知。我想它们属于曾。他从未给我任何书看。我不是共产党人，也不属于任何政党。

（签名）顾阿兴。

My name is Buh Tung. I am a native of Bangkok, Siam.
My father is Chinese, my mother Siamese. My home address is
1910, New Road, Bangkok. I arrived in Shanghai from Bangkok

but I do not know where it is located.

can only speak very little English. While I was at school,
many people told me that I could obtain an excellent education

October last year in order to come here. Between October

On January 2 I left Bangkok for Shanghai on a Butterfield

As this friend was familiar with the voyage, my father
requested him to escort me to Shanghai, and my father paid
both the fares. We arrived in Shanghai on January 9. Upon
arrival my father's friend took me to the hotel and stayed

西虹口 1934年1月13日 翻译 朱 (Tsu)。

我叫向敦。我是暹罗曼谷人。我的父亲是中国人，母亲是暹罗人。我的家庭住址是曼谷新路（New Road）1910号。我三天前从曼谷抵达上海，此后一直住在一家旅馆里，但我不知道它位于何处。

我于1917年出生在上述地址，我的父亲在那里开设并至今经营着一家药店。8岁时，我开始在曼谷的元明小学（Yuen Ming Primary School，音译）读书。我在那里一直待到13岁。在那个年龄，我开始在同样位于曼谷的本妙中学（Bun Myoch Middle School，音译）读书，并在那里待了4年，直到1933年10月。在这些学校就读期间，我学习了中文、英语语法、地理、历史、数学和暹罗语。我能读写中文和暹罗语。我只能说很少的英语。当我在学校时，许多人告诉我，如果我来上海，可以接受极好的英语教育。因此，我于去年10月离校以便来这里。在10月至1月2日之间，我安静地在家中和父母待在一起。1月2日，我乘坐宝丰洋行（Butterfield & Swire）的一艘轮船离开曼谷前往上海，船名我已忘记。陪同我的是我父亲的一位朋友向傲（Bah Ngao，音译），他在暹罗清拜县（Tsing Pai Hsien，音译）也开了一家药店。由于这位朋友熟悉航程，我父亲请求他护送我到上海，我父亲支付了两人的路费。我们于1月9日抵达上海。抵达后，我父亲的朋友带我去了旅馆并陪伴

我直到1月11日，随后他返回曼谷。离开前，他给了我一封信，让我交给住在海宁路945弄2338号（原文如此，前文为1338号）的一名叫宗（Zung）(    ) 的男子，还给了我400美元，这是我父亲托付给他用于我教育的费用。我今天早上8点去了宗的家，把信和400美元交给了他。宗让我留在那里。他上午10点出去，没有回来。我中午12点出去吃午饭，下午1点回到住处。我一直待在屋里，直到被捕。宗给了我一件大衣，口袋里发现的公园季票和其他物品都属于宗。

（签名）纳敦 (Nah Tung，注：此处签名与上文名字Buh Tung拼写略有差异，照实译出)。

Woo Zung Ching (□□□)
Wenchow                                      D.S. McKeown
W.Hongkew           13-1-34                  Clerk Wang Kuo Lian

My name is Woo Zung Ching, age 27, native of Wenchow.
I reside at 34 Tsu Ka Jao, Pootung. I am a farmer by
occupation, but being unemployed and knowing that a man
named Zung Ts Yee (鄭子儀), who was my friend at Wenchow,
was an agent of the Nanking Government, I visited him at
5 p.m. January 12 to find out if he could obtain employment
for me. Zung told me to wait in his room as he was
expecting two or three communists to come and asked me to
watch them when they arrived. At 6 p.m. a female arrived
and shortly afterwards a Siamese came and later a male
Chinese also came. On the pretext of ordering food Zung
left the room at 7 p.m. and I locked the door (as pre-
arranged). When he left the room, I remained with the
3 people in the room until the Police arrived.

(Signed) Woo Zung Ching.

吴仁卿 (Woo Zung Ching)
温州                                      侦探长 麦基翁 (D.S. McKeown)
西虹口           1934年1月13日                  书记员 王国连 (Wang Kuo Lian)

我叫吴仁卿，27岁，温州人。我居住在浦东曹家宅（Tsu Ka Jao，音译）34号。我的职业是农民，但由于失业，且知道一位名叫郑子仪（Zung Ts Yee）的人是我在温州时的朋友，也是南京政府的代理人，我于1月12日下午5点拜访他，想看看他能否为我找到工作。郑让我在他的房间里等候，因为他预计会有两三个共产党人来，并让我在他们到达时监视他们。下午6点，一名女性到达，不久后一名暹罗人到来，随后一名中国男性也来了。晚上7点，郑以订购食物为借口离开了房间，我锁上了门（按事先约定）。当他离开房间后，我和那3个人留在房间里，直到警察到达。

（签名）吴仁卿。
